- issues opened in `story-repo`#6 ("Results of E1-E7 for claims C1-C7 (experiment-repo, first complete pass)") by `experiment-repo`  > Results for the Outline claims, from `experiment-repo` `main` (tables in `results/`, also in paper-repo `dev`; `results/headline.csv` is new). Everything below is a measurement on the stated cells; E3 disjoint-draw and the T2 reference cells (n = 500 on census/alphafold) are still running, so Table 3 / the B5 headline rows are not final. Reference n = 500 (forest N = 1000, ballots N = 5000, others N = 8000–10000).
  > 
  > **C2 (headroom, real data; headline arm A6 `select`, margin as pre-fixed).** At n = 500, 8 of 9 sets are "no gain" (ratio CI inside [0.98, 1.02]); gene_expression is "small / undecided" (r = 0.971, label saving 5.7%). Ratios: alphafold 1.000, ballots 1.000, census_education 1.005, census_healthcare 1.003, census_income 0.992, forest 1.001, galaxies 1.003, plankton 1.001. Estimated-floor ratios (A7, within the spline class) are 0.993–1.005. One cell wins the pre-fixed gain rule: gene_expression n = 100 (r = 0.930 [0.929, 0.932], coverage 0.951, valid), with the floor ratio 0.989, i.e. the floor estimated within a model class is not a ceiling there (the selected flexible calibrator beats it). So the headline reads "PPI++ is near the floor on 8 of 9 sets at n ≥ 300; the exception is gene_expression". At n ∈ {30, 100} A6 is mostly wider than PPI++ (median r = 1.017, range 0.917–1.116), at n ≥ 1000 r is 0.992–1.002.
  > 
  > **C3 (break-even).** Predicted n* (K/(K−1)·d_eff·σ²_res/Δ; PPI++ learning cost included in `pred_nstar_net`) is within factor 3 of the measured grid bracket in 115 of 127 cells with a prediction (synthetic quad n-sweep 35/35, shapes 12/12, reference 45/51, stress-transform 23/29). Exceptions concentrate on gene_expression and census_income_log. Break-even is validity-conditioned (cells where the arm undercovers are censored, not counted as crossings).
  > 
  > **C4 (validity).** A6 coverage, reference grid: n ≥ 300 median 0.948 (min 0.925); `valid_vs_ppipp` = 1 in all cells with n ≥ 300; strict `valid` is 0.89 at n 300–500 and 0.17 at n 30–100, because Wald intervals of PPI++ itself undercover at n ≤ 100 (A6 coverage median 0.927 at n 30–100, min 0.806 ballots). Some apparent small-n gains are undercoverage artefacts (ballots n = 30: r = 0.93, coverage 0.806, invalid). The with-replacement vs disjoint-draw check (E3, 6 cells × 3 arms) gives the same widths and ratios (within about 1%); coverage differs by ≤ 0.012 except galaxies at n = 1000/3000, where disjoint draws overcover (0.97–0.98), consistent with a finite-population effect (my interpretation, not separately tested).
  > 
  > **C1/E2.** The excess of the oracle linear estimator matches (1/n − 1/M)Δ (median measured/predicted 0.98); in-sample PPI++ pays 1.6–2.3× the leading learning cost at small n. PPI++ vs pooled linear: width ratio 0.983–1.002 (approximately equal, not identical: the package SE differs from the pooled-sample SE).
  > 
  > **C5 (constructions, binary Y, n = 25–200).** Wilson/t/Wald/truncation change coverage by 1–3 points at small n and change the PPI++-relative ratio by ≤ 1–2%; no construction rescues small-n coverage for the control-variate estimators (alphafold n = 25: Wald 0.82, Wilson 0.83 for A6; labels-only Wilson 0.966). Bootstrap-t is worse (undercovers, e.g. 0.74 at alphafold n = 25).
  > 
  > **C6 (X).** Real sets (census ×3, alphafold; n = 200/1000): no gain from X: `select_x` r 0.999–1.024, `gbm_aipw` worse (1.02–1.11) — a null result. Synthetic positive control (E6 synth, 12 cells): when X carries linear signal (t1 = 0.6) the vector PPI++/OLS arms reach r ≈ 0.85–0.93 at valid coverage, and `select_x` follows (r 0.81–0.90 with both signals); when X carries only a nonlinear signal GBM-AIPW/`select_x` give 0.86–0.88 where linear arms give 1.00; with no signal all arms are 1.00–1.03. So the pipeline detects X-gains when they exist; the real sets simply have none beyond f.
